preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(row, list) and all(isinstance(cell, int) and cell in {0, 1} for cell in row) for row in matrix)
preconditions.description: The input matrix is a rectangular 2D list where each cell is either 0 (landmine) or 1 (safe).
The matrix is non-empty and has at least one row and one column.

preconditions.expression: all(len(row) == len(matrix[0]) for row in matrix)
preconditions.description: All rows in the matrix have the same length (rectangular).

postconditions.description: If no safe path exists, return -1. Otherwise, return the length of the shortest safe path (number of steps) from any cell in the first column to any cell in the last column, where the path avoids landmines and their four adjacent cells.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= i < len(matrix) and 0 <= j < len(matrix[0]) and matrix[i][j] == 1 for i, j in [(0, 0), (len(matrix) - 1, len(matrix[0]) - 1)]) or return_value == -1
postconditions.description: If the start (first column) or end (last column) cells are all landmines, return -1 (no valid path).

postconditions.expression: any(matrix[i][0] == 1 for i in range(len(matrix))) and any(matrix[i][len(matrix[0]) - 1] == 1 for i in range(len(matrix))) or return_value == -1
postconditions.description: The first or last column must contain at least one safe cell (1) for a valid path to exist.

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 or (return_value == min(possible_paths) if possible_paths else -1)
postconditions.description: The returned value is the minimum length of all valid safe paths from any cell in the first column to any cell in the last column, where a path is defined as a sequence of adjacent (up, down, left, right) safe cells (1) that avoids landmines and their four adjacent cells.
